Docs/ Theme development/Your first theme

Your first theme

Build a theme package from a directory, zip it, upload it and activate it.

A theme package is a directory with no code in it:

starter/
  theme.json          metadata, widget areas, menus, styles, customizer options
  templates/          Go html/template files
    index.html
    single.html
    page.html
    header.html
    footer.html
  assets/
    style.css
    screenshot.png
  readme.md           optional, shown on the marketplace page

1. theme.json

The minimum:

{
  "slug": "starter",
  "name": "Starter",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "description": "A minimal starting point.",
  "author": "Gopher Co.",
  "screenshot": "screenshot.png",
  "menu_locations": [{"id": "primary", "name": "Primary Menu"}],
  "widget_areas": [{"id": "sidebar-1", "name": "Sidebar", "description": "Appears on the right."}],
  "styles": [{"handle": "starter-style", "src": "assets/style.css"}]
}

Every field is described on the theme.json page.

2. Templates

templates/index.html is the only required template; the others fall back to it along the WordPress hierarchy (templates). A complete index.html for the blog:

{{template "header" .}}
<main id="main" class="site-main">
{{range .Posts}}
  <article id="post-{{.ID}}" class="{{.Class}}">
    <h2 class="entry-title"><a href="{{.Permalink}}">{{.Title}}</a></h2>
    <div class="entry-meta">{{.EntryMeta}}</div>
    <div class="entry-content">{{if .ShowExcerpt}}{{.Excerpt}}{{else}}{{.Content}}{{end}}</div>
  </article>
{{else}}
  <p>Nothing found.</p>
{{end}}
{{.Pagination}}
</main>
{{template "footer" .}}

header.html and footer.html define the parts the pages include:

{{define "header"}}<!doctype html>
<html lang="en-US">
<head>
<meta charset="UTF-8">
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
<title>{{.DocumentTitle}}</title>
{{.Head}}
</head>
<body class="{{.BodyClass}}">
{{.BodyOpen}}
<header class="site-header">
  {{.CustomLogo}}
  <p class="site-title"><a href="{{.HomeURL}}" rel="home">{{.SiteName}}</a></p>
  <p class="site-description">{{.Description}}</p>
  {{with index .Menus "primary"}}<nav aria-label="Primary"><ul class="menu">
    {{range .}}<li class="menu-item{{if .Current}} current-menu-item{{end}}"><a href="{{.URL}}">{{.Label}}</a></li>{{end}}
  </ul></nav>{{end}}
</header>
{{end}}

{{define "footer"}}
{{with index .Areas "sidebar-1"}}<aside class="widget-area">{{.}}</aside>{{end}}
<footer class="site-footer">{{.PrivacyLink}}</footer>
{{.Footer}}{{.AdminBar}}
</body>
</html>
{{end}}

{{.Head}} prints wp_head() (feeds, block styles, your enqueued styles, the Customizer's CSS, plugin assets) and {{.Footer}} prints wp_footer(). Leave them in: without them scripts, the admin bar and plugins do not work.

3. Assets

Put style.css, scripts, fonts and images under assets/ and reference them from theme.json (styles, scripts, preload_fonts, editor_styles). screenshot.png (1200×900) is the Themes screen thumbnail.

4. Zip it

cd starter
zip -r ../starter.zip theme.json templates assets readme.md

The files sit at the zip root (a single top-level folder is also accepted and stripped). Limits: 32 MiB per package, 4 MiB per file, and only these extensions: .json .html .css .js .map .svg .png .jpg .jpeg .gif .webp .avif .ico .woff .woff2 .ttf .otf .md .txt.

5. Upload and activate

Appearance › Themes › Add Theme › Upload Theme, choose starter.zip. The package is validated (theme.json, template syntax, file types), unpacked to <data>/themes/starter/ and listed on the Themes screen. Live Preview shows it without activating; Activate switches the site. A package whose slug matches a bundled theme is rejected.

6. Iterate

Either upload again, or edit in place with Appearance › Theme File Editor — the overlay directory is the same <data>/themes/starter/ the installer wrote to (file editor). During development point WPGO_THEMES_DIR at your working copy: the server loads every <dir>/<slug>/theme.json at start-up.
